question: Which act was enacted for the decentralization of Madras Province and Bombay Province?  (RPF SI(06/01/2019) Shift 3)
options: Act of 1858 for Better Governance
Morley-Minto Correction, 1909
Montagu Chelmsford Reforms, 1919
Indian Council Act 1861
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Indian Council Act 1861

Explanation:
The Indian Council Act 1861 was enacted by the British Parliament. This act brought decentralization to the Madras and Bombay provinces, granting them legislative powers. Under this act, provincial councils were formed, including Indian members, though their role was limited. It was part of administrative reforms after the Revolt of 1857. This act marked the first step towards decentralization in India, giving provinces autonomy in certain internal matters.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Which act is known for decentralization of Madras and Bombay? → Indian Council Act 1861
☛ What system did this act introduce? → Introduction of provincial legislative councils
☛ What was the objective of this act? → To include Indians in administration after the 1857 revolt
☛ Under which Viceroy was this act passed? → Lord Canning
☛ What does decentralization mean? → Transfer of powers from center to provinces
question_hi: मद्रास प्रांत और बॉम्बे प्रांत के विकेंद्रीकरण के लिए कौन सा अधिनियम बनाया गया था? (RPF SI(06/01/2019) Shift 3)
options_hi: बेहतर शासन के लिए 1858 का अधिनियम
मॉर्ले-मिंटो सुधार, 1909
मोंटागु चेम्सफोर्ड सुधार, 1919

solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है भारतीय परिषद अधिनियम 1861

Explanation:
भारतीय परिषद अधिनियम 1861 को ब्रिटिश संसद द्वारा पारित किया गया था। इस अधिनियम ने मद्रास और बॉम्बे प्रांतों में विकेंद्रीकरण लाया, जिससे इन प्रांतों को विधायी शक्तियाँ प्रदान हुईं। इस अधिनियम के तहत प्रांतीय परिषदों का गठन किया गया, जिसमें भारतीयों को शामिल किया गया, हालांकि उनकी भूमिका सीमित थी। यह अधिनियम 1857 के विद्रोह के बाद प्रशासनिक सुधारों का हिस्सा था। इसने भारत में विकेंद्रीकरण की दिशा में पहला कदम रखा और प्रांतों को कुछ आंतरिक मामलों में स्वायत्तता दी।

question: According to the Child Labour Prevention Act (Amendment) 2016, child labour is prohibited below the age of________years. (RPF SI(06/01/2019) Shift 3)
options: 14
16
18
7
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 14

Explanation:
According to the Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Amendment Act, 2016, child labour is prohibited for children below the age of 14 years. This amendment strictly bans employment of children in any occupation and also prohibits adolescents (14-18 years) from working in hazardous occupations. For the first time, the act introduced the category of 'adolescent' and allows them to work only in non-hazardous occupations. However, helping family businesses after school hours or during vacations is not considered an offense. The act aims to ensure that children get access to education and a healthy development. It also aligns with the Right to Education Act, making 14 years the key age for compulsory education.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Minimum age for child labour prohibition under 2016 Act → 14 years
☛ Age group defined as adolescent → 14 to 18 years
☛ Hazardous occupations banned for → persons below 18 years
☛ Exception for family business → allowed after school hours or vacations
☛ Main objective of the Act → Ensure education and development of children

question: Has the President of India declared a ﬁnancial emergency thus far? (RPF SI(06/01/2019) Shift 1)
options: Never Announced
Yes, only once
Yes, two times
Yes, three times
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Never Announced

Explanation:
The President of India has never declared a Financial Emergency (Article 360) so far. This provision is part of the Indian Constitution but has never been used. Financial Emergency can be proclaimed when the financial stability or credit of the nation is threatened. During such an emergency, the central government can interfere in the financial matters of states. While President's Rule (Article 356) and National Emergency (Article 352) have been invoked several times, the Financial Emergency has never been imposed.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Which Article deals with Financial Emergency? → Article 360
☛ When is Financial Emergency imposed? → When the financial stability or credit of India is threatened
☛ What happens during Financial Emergency? → Centre controls state finances
☛ How many times has Financial Emergency been imposed so far? → Never
☛ What are the other types of emergencies? → National (Article 352) and President's Rule (Article 356)
question_hi: क्या भारत के राष्ट्रपति ने अब तक कभी वित्तीय आपातकाल की घोषणा की है? (RPF SI(06/01/2019) Shift 1)

Explanation:
भारत के राष्ट्रपति ने अब तक कभी भी वित्तीय आपातकाल (अनुच्छेद 360) की घोषणा नहीं की है। यह प्रावधान भारतीय संविधान में शामिल है, लेकिन आज तक इसका उपयोग नहीं हुआ। वित्तीय आपातकाल की घोषणा तब की जा सकती है जब देश की वित्तीय स्थिरता या साख को खतरा हो। इस दौरान केंद्र सरकार राज्यों के वित्तीय मामलों में हस्तक्षेप कर सकती है। राष्ट्रपति शासन (अनुच्छेद 356) और राष्ट्रीय आपातकाल (अनुच्छेद 352) का उपयोग कई बार हुआ है, लेकिन वित्तीय आपातकाल कभी लागू नहीं किया गया।

question: Which schedule of constitution gives the list of states and union territories?  (RPF SI(06/01/2019) Shift 1)
options: Tenth Schedule
Second Schedule
Seventh Schedule
First Schedule
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is First Schedule

Explanation:
The First Schedule of the Indian Constitution provides the list of states and union territories along with their territories. It is covered under Articles 1 and 4 of the Constitution. Originally, it contained 29 states and 7 union territories, but after several amendments, there are now 28 states and 8 union territories. The Tenth Schedule deals with anti-defection law, the Second Schedule specifies salaries and allowances of the President, Governors, Chief Justice, etc., and the Seventh Schedule contains the Union, State, and Concurrent lists. Thus, the First Schedule is the correct answer as it directly lists the states and union territories.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ What is in the First Schedule? → List and territories of states and UTs
☛ Which articles relate to the First Schedule? → Articles 1 and 4
☛ Which schedule deals with anti-defection? → Tenth Schedule
☛ What does the Second Schedule contain? → Salaries of President, Governor, etc.
☛ What is in the Seventh Schedule? → Union, State, and Concurrent lists

question: How much is the tenure of Chief Election Commissioner's oﬃce (RPF SI(06/01/2019) Shift 1)
options: Six years
Three years
Five years
Four years
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Six years

Explanation:
The tenure of the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) of India is six years or until the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier. This provision is made under Article 324 of the Indian Constitution. They head the Election Commission of India and are responsible for conducting free and fair elections in the country. The appointment is made by the President.

question: Which of the following languages has been declared as the oﬃcial language of the Government of India?  (RPF SI(06/01/2019) Shift 1)
options: Bengali
Telugu
Tamil
Hindi
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Hindi

Explanation:
According to Article 343(1) of the Indian Constitution, Hindi written in Devanagari script is the official language of the Government of India. This provision came into effect on 26 January 1965. Under the Official Language Act, 1963 and its amendments, English is recognized as a co-official language alongside Hindi. Articles 346 and 347 lay down rules for communication between states and the Centre. The Eighth Schedule of the Constitution lists 22 languages, but only Hindi is the official language of the Union. Hence, option 4 is correct.

☛ Script of Hindi → Devanagari
☛ Year Hindi was declared official language → 1965

question: Which of the following parts of the Indian Constitution contains the provision of emergency? (RPF SI(06/01/2019) Shift 2)

solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Part XVIII (Eighteen)

Explanation:
The Part XVIII (Eighteen) of the Indian Constitution deals with emergency provisions. It describes three types of emergencies: National Emergency (Article 352), State Emergency or President's Rule (Article 356), and Financial Emergency (Article 360). National Emergency can be imposed on grounds of war, external aggression, or armed rebellion. State Emergency is imposed when the state government is unable to function according to the constitutional machinery. Financial Emergency is imposed when the financial stability of India is threatened. These provisions are covered under Articles 352 to 360 in Part XVIII. This part grants extensive powers to the central government during extraordinary circumstances.

question_hi: भारतीय संविधान के निम्नलिखित भागों में से किसमें आपातकाल का प्रावधान है? (RPF SI(06/01/2019) Shift 2)

question: The concept of the Supreme Court's Advisory jurisdiction was taken from which country?  (RPF SI(06/01/2019) Shift 2)
options: Japanese
Canada
British
Australian
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Canada

Explanation:
The concept of Advisory Jurisdiction of the Supreme Court of India was borrowed from Canada. Under Article 143, the President can seek the opinion of the Supreme Court on legal matters, but this opinion is not binding on the court. This provision exists in the Canadian Constitution where the Supreme Court of Canada has the authority to give opinions on questions referred by the government. India adopted this concept to enable the President to obtain judicial advice on disputes between the Centre and states or on important legal questions, aiding in their resolution.

question: Who appoints the Chief Justice of India? (RPF SI(06/01/2019) Shift 2)
options: Union Home Minister
Prime Minister
President
Parliamentary Committee
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is President

Explanation:
According to Article 124 of the Indian Constitution, the President appoints the Chief Justice of India. This process is designed to ensure the independence of the judiciary. The Chief Justice holds office until the age of 65. The Prime Minister or Home Minister do not directly appoint; they only recommend. A Parliamentary Committee is not involved in the appointment.

question: The concept of social, economic and political justice has been taken from which revolution? (RPF SI(06/01/2019) Shift 2)

question: Who is considered the last bastion of the democracy? (RPF SI(06/01/2019) Shift 2)

Unlike the parliament and executive, the judiciary is independent and impartial, which helps maintain democratic values.

question: Which states are included in the Mahadayi Water Disputes Tribunal?  (RPF SI(06/01/2019) Shift 2)
options: Odisha, Telangana and Andhra Pradesh
Goa, Gujarat and Maharashtra
Gujarat, Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh
Goa, Karnataka and Maharashtra
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Goa, Karnataka and Maharashtra

Explanation:
The Mahadayi Water Disputes Tribunal was constituted to resolve the water-sharing dispute of the Mahadayi River (also known as Mandovi). This river originates in the Western Ghats and flows into the Arabian Sea. The dispute primarily involves the states of Goa, Karnataka, and Maharashtra. Karnataka proposed the Kalasa-Bhandura dam project on the river, which was opposed by Goa. The tribunal delivered its final verdict in 2018, allocating 13.42 TMC water to Karnataka, 24 TMC to Goa, and 1.33 TMC to Maharashtra. The river is the lifeline of Goa, serving as the main source of drinking water and irrigation for the state.

question: Who is the caretaker President of India in the absence of the President?  (RPF SI(06/01/2019) Shift 2)
options: Speaker of Lok Sabha
The most senior member of the Rajya Sabha
Chief Justice of India
Vice-President
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Vice-President

Explanation:
According to Article 65 of the Indian Constitution, in the absence, death, or removal of the President, the Vice-President acts as the caretaker President. This constitutional arrangement is a crucial part of India's democratic framework. It is important to note that the Speaker of Lok Sabha, the most senior member of Rajya Sabha, or the Chief Justice of India are not authorized for this role.

question: Without sanctioning a bill by the President and not returning it, it is called __________, to be kept pending for an indeﬁnite period of time. (RPF SI(06/01/2019) Shift 2)
options: Suspicious Veto
Absolute Veto
Qualiﬁed Veto
Pocket Veto
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Pocket Veto

Explanation:
When the President neither approves a bill nor returns it, but keeps it pending for an indefinite period, it is called Pocket Veto. This concept is borrowed from the US Constitution. Under Article 111 of the Indian Constitution, the President has three options: give assent, return the bill, or withhold it. In Pocket Veto, the President takes no action, leaving the bill in abeyance. This power is particularly useful when the government is in a minority or the bill is constitutionally questionable. Suspensive Veto involves returning the bill for reconsideration, Absolute Veto means outright rejection, and Qualified Veto is used only in some countries.

question: The provision of the joint sitting of the two houses of Parliament has been taken from which constitution? (RPF SI 2018 (06/01/2019) Shift 3)

French Constitution
Australian Constitution
Irish Constitution
solution:

Explanation:
The provision of joint sitting of both houses of Parliament in the Indian Constitution is taken from the Australian Constitution. It aims to resolve a deadlock on a bill when there is disagreement between Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha. This provision is inspired by the Australian Constitution, which also has a mechanism for joint sittings to resolve disagreements between the two houses.
